answer: Each applicant is assigned one tree in a grove, tended by an arborist. Each round the registry names a branch to cut; the holder cuts it, and a falcon flies over the meadow to photograph it, whose growth rings are checked against its record. The next branch is picked from the ring pattern plus the key, so cuts arrive in sequence and no cut fits another tree. A further identity needs another tree, arborist, and falcon flight: $290 and one arborist-day. 5,000 fakes cost $1.45 million and 5,000 arborist-days; one arborist cannot tend two groves at once, and no two trees share rings.
